summary: H.R. 5966 amends the Federal Water Pollution Control Act to create the Ohio River Basin Restoration Program and an Ohio River National Program Office within the Environmental Protection Agency. The program is designed to oversee large-scale environmental restoration, water quality improvements, flood resilience, and habitat protection across the Ohio River Basin.

affected_groups.effect: Must establish the program office, appoint a Program Director, develop actionable goals and action plans, manage grants, submit annual reports, and include the program as a separate budget line item.
Eligible to receive grants and enter agreements to plan, design, implement, or construct restoration projects and activities.
Engaged and consulted early in the development of actionable goals and action plans through coordination with the Bureau of Indian Affairs and representation on the advisory council.

key_provisions: Establishes the Ohio River National Program Office within the Environmental Protection Agency, led by an appointed Program Director.
Requires the Program Director to create measurable actionable goals within one year and a comprehensive action plan within two years, with updates every five years.
Creates an advisory council consisting of federal entities, state representatives from the basin, basin regions, tribal governments, and the Ohio River Valley Water Sanitation Commission.
Authorizes grants and agreements for non-federal entities, including state, regional, local, and tribal governments, educational institutions, and nonprofits to carry out restoration projects.
Authorizes appropriations of $350,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2030 to carry out the program.
Mandates annual reporting to Congress and public websites regarding program progress, fund transfers, grants, and specific projects.
missing_information: The bill text does not specify exact matching fund requirements or cost-share percentages for non-federal grant recipients.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 5966 amends the Federal Water Pollution Control Act to create the Ohio River Basin Restoration Program and an Ohio River National Program Office within the Environmental Protection Agency. The program is designed to oversee large-scale environmental restoration, water quality improvements, flood resilience, and habitat protection across the Ohio River Basin.
summary_detail.significance: This bill establishes a formal, coordinated federal restoration program for the Ohio River Basin backed by an authorized funding level of $350 million annually for fiscal years 2026 through 2030, aiming to improve water quality, habitats, and community resilience across multiple states.
